correctness.rationale: For m>=2,k>=3, write L=L_{K_m}⊗I+I⊗L_star and G=(mI+L_star)^{-1}. A horizontal unit edge has potential (e_i−e_j)⊗G e_s, yielding its absolute clique and spoke voltage-drop column sums. A vertical unit spoke splits into a constant-in-clique tree mode plus (e_i−1/m 1)⊗G(e_0−e_ell). The derived inverse entries have fixed positive signs and 0<a<1, so all absolute values are resolved algebraically. P=I−Q gives each cycle column norm as 1+cut_column_norm−2Q_ee. Subtractions q_h−q_l>0 and p_h−p_l>0 exclude leaf maxima. Integer sign polynomials A_Q and A_P give the exact hub/spoke boundaries: Q tie m=4,k=11; P ties m=7,k=11 and m=8,k=37, and switch at m=6 k=5. An independent grounded-Laplacian numerical reconstruction on 64 (m,k) instances independently tested three edge columns per case, 192 in total; largest six-column formula error was 5.33e−15. The universal proof is symbolic matrix inversion and sign analysis, not the finite grid.
